figures.label: From storm report to your roof

art_direction.identity: A roofer's website written like a weather service bulletin: cool sky-paper canvas, storm-slate ink, deep storm-navy fields, and radar-legend colour used only where it carries data. Rounded-small corners, hairline rules, bright daylight photographs of finished roofs.
art_direction.type: Familjen Grotesk (600) for every heading, tight tracking; Figtree for everything else at 1rem/1.65. Timestamps and readings use the bulletin utility with tabular numerals. Never a third family.
art_direction.color: Canvas #eef2f5, surface #ffffff, ink #0e1a26, muted #4b5b6a, hairline #cfd8e0, storm field #12263a. Radar green (bg-primary) is the one action colour — buttons and one focal mark per section, never text. The five radar colours appear only in the storm map and hail legend.
art_direction.signature: The storm log — a drawn hail-swath map over the service area's street grid, the radar bands blooming from green to magenta, with a bulletin readout of the storm and how many roofs the crew checked after it.
art_direction.voice: A calm crew lead after a hailstorm. Plain facts, real numbers, dates and times. No 'quality craftsmanship', no exclamation points, never fear-selling.
